svg.title: Field lines and equipotentials of a charged insulating rod
svg.desc: Two computed panels for a diagonal insulating rod whose positive charges are crowded near its upper-right end, with a few in the middle and one at the lower-left end. (a) Field lines start on the charges and run outward; they are dense near the heavily charged end, and lines from the middle and lower parts tilt away from that end instead of leaving at right angles. (b) Equipotentials: small, closely spaced loops wrap the heavily charged end; the lower contours cross the rod, because an insulator surface is not an equipotential; farther out the contours become larger, rounder closed curves around the whole rod. The potential increases toward the rod and is highest at the heavily charged end. Equipotentials and field lines cross at right angles.
